# Selected next trial: private identical carrier tail and immutable key metadata

**Selected 31 October 2026 UTC, after the complete reader trial and renewed primary-source research; before any codec source edit.** Choose **C1-P + C2**. This is a bounded optimization hypothesis, not a speedup, item-2 acceptance, permission to skip validation, or production-readiness claim. A writer may start only after the coordinator verifies this decision/research and the complete reader raw checkpoint on private research-reference, then sends an explicit ownership handoff.

## Why this next step

The published reader-only source `ae50094cd242c4d46950f8a9a99d1ecdca03b7f8` passes full correctness. Its complete, independently checked reader trial retains accepted-item1 version-pair costs: float256 query/JSON paired medians 1.0878/1.0833 and wide query/JSON 1.1162/1.1192, all four descriptive intervals above 1; mixed64 JSON is 1.0535. Same-artifact reader-versus-FFC estimates are modest, not full recovery. All 168 timed processes /11,760 checksum-counter outcomes, 56 full untimed payloads and separate profiles are preserved. Root separately reconstructs every 1,176 pair row, 28 summaries/strata and 560,000 bootstrap medians; an independent implementation checks captured exits/provenance/outcomes and bounded negatives without importing study validators.

Fresh profiles establish repeated per-cell work, not its exclusive latency: current wide output has 2,048 cells /1,024 floats, with 2,049 `_native_keys` and 2,048 `_carrier_payload` calls per public query. Fixed FP observation remains six/query or seven/query_json. Fresh CPython evidence refines the mechanism: literal sets can use cached constant hashes and copy/merge paths. Removing source-level set constructions does not measure malloc/free events, five fresh hashes per literal, cycles, or a speedup. The DuckDB Python driver has already recursively boxed the nested result before this private converter; this is not native vectorization or late materialization.

The earlier C1-S option shared the after-key tail with the public wrapper. Prefer C1-P instead: preserve the public function entirely verbatim and duplicate only its small payload-shape tail privately. It removes the same private work without adding a public helper frame, dispatch or recursion depth. The explicit maintenance cost is tiny duplicated shape logic, bound by an actual-suite AST identity test. `_canonical_payload` remains the single shared domain/finite/zero implementation. Source line numbers and global allocation/GC schedules are not promised identical.

## Exact implementation boundary

1. Keep the entire public `_carrier_payload` function text verbatim: exact-dict/key gate, literal set, payload tail, diagnostics and both selected-slot accesses. Do not narrow its ordinary custom-key acceptance or route it through another helper.
2. Add one private after-key helper, taking `value`, with the identical public body tail after its first key gate. Ignore only a helper docstring when comparing body ASTs. Preserve tag access/type/range, selected-slot computation, first selected nonnull lookup, unused-NULL generator and short-circuit ordering, and final selected-slot lookup/return. Do not cache the selected payload: ordinary key equality during an unused-slot lookup can change it.
3. Call this private helper from exactly one intended application site, `_native_result_wire`, immediately after the existing `_native_keys(cell, expected)` admission. Its premise is this private caller's exact dict, all keys exact built-in strings, and complete five-field keyset admission. It is not a token, public bypass, ambient checked state or permission cache.
4. Keep `_native_keys` runtime body unchanged: exact-dict check, complete exact-string screen BEFORE view comparison, then matching fields. Only its expected-container annotation may be made accurate for immutable metadata.
5. Hoist exactly two private schema sets into module-level `frozenset` values of exact built-in strings: root `rows/rounds/derived_facts/work`, and carrier `tag/s/b/i/f`. Use them only at the two existing private call sites. Public carrier/JSON/constructor gates remain untouched. These are immutable schema metadata, not immutable module bindings or FP permissions.
6. Keep selected-payload exact-type checking and `_canonical_payload(tag, payload, _copy_float_bits)` unchanged. No generator rewrite, ASCII shortcut, alternate float classifier, tuple-return rewrite, buffer reuse, in-place raw mutation, lazy result or unvalidated trust in native output.
7. Preserve all FP observation/guard locations and predicates, public independent admission, six-field Query snapshot/readiness, late `known_at=None` resolution, caps/root confinement, budgets, locks, transactions/rollback/receipts and eager no-prefix publication. Keep legacy, native, binding, schemas, browser and FP reader bytes unchanged.

The combined private mechanism removes **2C+1 temporary source-level expected-set constructions and C repeated carrier-key comparisons/views**, for C output cells, after module setup. It retains initial private key admission, generators, both payload/domain tuples, all domain/type/null/finite/zero checks, string validation, float copies, output containers and all 6/7 FP reads. Empty removes only one root set; fixed costs remain. No recovery forecast follows.
